findings.detail: The source has 61 couplets: s327 has 26, s328 has 28 and s329 has 7. They align 1:1, in order, with /1–/61. The parenthesized optional lines s327 L10–L11 are /10–/11. The wording differences, for example /40 מִזְבֵּחַ אֶבְנֶה בְּשִׁבְרוֹן לִבִּי against מזבח אבנים בשרי ולבי, fall inside a unit and do not move any boundary.

Both sides have 48 units, but their extents differ. The source couplet s330 L5 וְאַזְכִּיר טוּבְךָ וְצִדְקוֹתֶיךָ. חֲסָדֶיךָ וּגְבוּרוֹתֶיךָ has no canonical counterpart. Canonical /23 וּזְרוֹעֲךָ וֶאֱמוּנָתֶךָ אוֹדִיעַ כְּפִי גְדֻלָּתֶךָ does not appear in the source. Mapping by count would wrongly label L5 as /23. The verified mapping is: s329 Monday L1–18 = /1–18; s330 L1–4 = /19–22; L5 has no canonical unit; L6–28 = /24–46 (L27, in parentheses, = /45); s331 L1–2 = /47–48. /23 has no realization here.

The source has 78 couplets against 77 canonical units. s331 has 22 Tuesday couplets, one of them split over two lines; the compare-327 completeness note says 21, which is wrong. s332 has 28 and s333 has 28. s333 L2 (…דַּק מִמְּךָ נֶחְדָּל) = /52. s333 L3 וְאֵינְךָ נֶאֱצָל מִכֹּל וְנִבְדָּל. וְאֵין מָקוֹם רֵק מִמְּךָ וְנֶחְדָּל has no canonical unit. s332 L6 shares the first hemistich of /28, but its second hemistich is entirely different (לְבַדְּךָ תַּעֲשֶׂה וְאֵינְךָ נִלְאֶה against רחוק וקרוב ואינך נראה). The verified mapping is: s331 L1–22 = /1–22; s332 L1–28 = /23–50; s333 L1–2 = /51–52; L3 has no canonical unit; L4–28 = /53–77.

The source has 104 couplets against 103 canonical units. Canonical /6 אל ארך אפים is missing: s334 goes straight from /5 to /7. The parenthesized couplet s335 L6 (כְּדוֹב שַׁכּוּל וּכְנָמֵר שַׁחַל. כְּרָקָב וּכְעָשׁ וְרוּחוֹ כְּנָחַל) has no canonical unit. /50 is printed twice. s335 L24 sits at the canonical position, between /49 and /51, but with different wording (…עוֹשֶׂה אֵל נוֹרָא עֲלִילוֹת). s335 L28 has the /50 wording but comes after /53. /19 has its hemistichs reversed, and the second hemistich of /95 differs (כִּי יְדַבֵּר אֶל חֲסִידָיו שָׁלוֹם). Wednesday runs on through s337 L1–22 (= /82–103), under a Thursday running head.

The grouped extents were checked against the canonical text: /1 = s337 Thursday L1–3; /2 = s337 L4 + s338 L1–3; /3 = s338 L4–5; /4 = L6–8; /5 = L9–13; /6 = L14–17; /7 = L18–22; /8 = L23–26; /9 = s338 L27–28 + s339 L1–5; /10 = s339 L6–10; /11 = L11–15; /12 = L16–21; /13 = L22–25; /14 = s339 L26–28 + s340 L1–4; /15 = s340 L5–8; /16 = L9–11; /17 = L12–16. /2, /9 and /14 cross page breaks. The footnote mark * sits on כָּל, the first word of /17.

The source has 46 couplets: 22 on s341 and 24 on s342. They align in order with /1–/46. In /31 the hemistichs are reversed and the first is reworded (אָז בְּאֵין לְבוּשׁ… / עַד לֹא אוֹרַג…); this is a variant inside the unit. Thursday /17 ends exactly at the foot of s340, and s341 L1 opens with the /1 incipit. So the Friday boundary without an internal heading rests on canonical extent, not only on the running head.

The mapping is: /1 = s342 L1–2 + s343 L1; /2 = s343 L2–5; /3 = L6–9; /4 = L10–13; /5 = L14–17; /6 = L18–20; /7 = L21–23; /8 = L24–26; /9 = s343 L27–28 + s344 L1–2. /10–/14 are the five quotations in the s344 paragraph, in canonical order: 1 Chr 16:36, Dan 2:20, Neh 9:5, Ps 106:48 and 1 Chr 29:10. Each is a whole verse, and the introducers ככתוב/ונאמר belong to the poem units. The poem ends before the rule and the heading שיר הכבוד.

findings.subject: Sunday closing line
findings.detail: The closing line ברוך אתה יחיד ומיוחד ה׳ אחד ושמו אחד on s329 is unpointed and set in a different face. The same words appear inside fifth_day/6, both in the canonical text and in the source at s338 L17. So it is absent from first_day only. A text match would wrongly join it to fifth_day/6. The Thursday occurrence must stay inside /6 as words of the poem.

The 31 registered incipit stanza URNs (poem.jsonl lines 81–111) match the source 1:1. s344 has 10 (anim…vayyechezu) and s345 has 21 (ziqnah…yeerav). The source adds no stanza and has no verse after yeerav. The heading, the ark-opening instruction and Ps 24:7–10 come before the stanza anim.

findings.subject: Biblical quotations
findings.detail: The existing shabbat /10 text carries the citation (דברי הימים א׳ ו:לו). That citation is wrong (the verse is 1 Chr 16:36) and is not Heidenheim's text. The existing first_day/34 likewise carries (תהלים נ:ח). There is also a duplication risk inside the project: 1 Chr 29:10 (Vayevarekh David), Neh 9:5 and Ps 24:7–10 are probably printed elsewhere in the machzor. The rule is one canonical verse milestone per project, and no duplicate URN just because a text is printed again.

findings.subject: Evidence gaps
findings.detail: canonical-phrase-search.json has no hit for fourth_day, because the canonical text has acrostic-split letters (אֲ רוֹמֵם). It has none for sixth_day either: the query was יוצר כל הוא, but the canonical text reads יוצר הכל הוא. Those two identifications rest on labels and filenames plus the manual extent check in this review. I did not confirm registry records for the seven roots or their numeric parts; I could not search poem.jsonl in this review. anim_zemirot is confirmed.

findings.subject: Numeric parts
findings.detail: Under SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME's sub-division numbering, the numbers /n are the 1150 projects' own division. Sharing a number means the extents are the same only where that has been verified. F2–F4 show that this does not hold for every root.

findings.subject: Footnote placement
findings.detail: The Thursday footnote continues physically on s341, below the Friday text. Encoded inline at that point, it would fall inside the sixth_day /1–22 scopes and be attributed to Friday.

findings.subject: Day-of-week selection
findings.detail: (a) hebrew-day turns over at nightfall, so an evening compile selects the next day's poem. At bein hashmashot the feature holds two values, the condition is undecided, and all seven poems print with their rubrics. (b) If this book or rite calls for the whole cycle on some occasion (for example a Yom Kippur eve custom), selecting by day would wrongly suppress it; this has not been checked against Heidenheim. (c) The rubric text of an undecided condition is editorial; it must never appear in the documentary output. (d) The day-7 selection must cover the whole Shabbat root, including /10–/14, and must not touch the Anim Zemirot section that follows it. (e) Where the Sunday closing line falls under the conditions is undecided.

required_changes: Replace the bare reuse list with an explicit mapping table for each root (source scan and line to /n), using the extents in F1–F7. Do not derive a /n from a sequential count anywhere.

second_day: do not map s330 L5 to /23. Close the open part with a bare terminator milestone of the same unit before L5, and resume with /24 at L6. Record /23 as unrealized; that is a valid partial witness. Alternatively, register a named incipit sub-part such as /veazkir. Do not mint a new number.

third_day: put a terminator before s333 L3 so that it carries no /n, and resume /53 at s333 L4. Record that s332 L6 is mapped to /28 with a differing second hemistich, and get approval for that decision.

fourth_day: record /6 as unrealized. Put a terminator before s335 L6, which has no canonical counterpart. Give /50 exactly one milestone, and decide in writing whether it goes on L24 (canonical position) or L28 (canonical wording). The other copy gets a terminator, or @source only, never a second /50 corresp. Record the reversed hemistichs in /19 and the variant second hemistich in /95.
fifth_day: carry the grouped extents across the s337/s338, s338/s339 and s339/s340 page breaks with milestones, not page-bounded containers.

Sunday closing line: end the first_day /61 scope (with a terminator or the end of the root div) before the closing line. Put the line in its own unit outside the first_day root, with no corresp until an independent identity has been researched. Never resolve it to fifth_day/6 or transclude it from there. Any future identity must take the Thursday occurrence into account, under the rule to nest only what lives in one place.

Thursday footnote: make it a standOff note of type commentary whose target is a local tei:anchor before כָּל at the start of fifth_day/17 (with targetEnd if needed). Do not target the shared URN, which would attach Heidenheim's note to other witnesses' realizations. Keep it out of the Friday flow on s341. Do not transcribe the * mark as poem text.

Friday: the bilingual editorial heading in the expanded output must be marked as supplied or editorial and left out of the documentary output. The boundary justification is canonical extent (F6), recorded in the README.

Shabbat /10–/14: put each quotation in a tei:seg type="quotation", with chapter/verse milestones placed inside the seg carrying canonical @n values. Keep the poem part milestones and the ככתוב/ונאמר introducers outside the seg, and close the inner scopes before the seg ends. Take the references from the canonical Bible (1 Chr 16:36, not ו:לו). Do not import any of the 1150 projects' parenthetical citations.

Before giving any canonical bible: corresp to 1 Chr 16:36, Dan 2:20, Neh 9:5, Ps 106:48, 1 Chr 29:10 or Ps 24:7–10, check whether the project already maps that verse elsewhere. If it does, use @source or a contextual quotation identity instead of a duplicate canonical corresp.

Shir HaKavod section: one division, in this order: the heading, then the instruction, then Ps 24:7–10 as a separate preparatory unit with verse-level milestones only (no chapter psalms/24 corresp, since only 4 verses are quoted), then the anim_zemirot root starting at stanza anim. The anim_zemirot scope must not include the heading, the instruction or the psalm.

Weekly cycle: the container is a registered siddur: unit (under hosafot or the agreed occasion) that holds only headings and transclusions. It is not a poem: or prayer: identity, and the seven roots are not nested under it.

Day selection: put the opensiddur:day-of-week hebrew-day conditionals only on the seven transclusions in the expanded book's arrangement. Never put them on the shared roots, in the Heidenheim source files, or on any ancestor shared with other services, and never in a book-level declaration. No range transclusion may cross into neighboring material.

Day selection: the Shabbat condition covers the whole Shabbat root including /10–/14. The Shir HaKavod section stays outside every daily condition and keeps its place after the Shabbat poem in source order. Decide explicitly where the Sunday closing line sits relative to the Sunday condition.

Day selection: confirm whether Heidenheim or the rite calls for the whole cycle on any occasion. If so, condition the selection so the whole cycle is kept then. Document how selection behaves after nightfall and at twilight.
Documentary output: it carries no day conditionals and prints no editorial rubrics or headings, only the source headings (שיר היחוד ליום ראשון., ליום שני., …, ליום השבת.).

Run urn_registry --check and confirm that all seven roots and every numeric part used are registered. Strip acrostic segmentation before incipit matching, and add verified incipit hits for fourth_day and sixth_day to the evidence.

Normalize the inconsistent work keys in the compare files (shir_hayihud_sunday, shir-hayihud-tuesday, friday, shabbat, shir_hakavod) to the canonical root URNs in the working data. Correct the Tuesday couplet count noted against s331.

The numeric-part mappings for first_day, fifth_day, sixth_day and day_of_shabbat are verified as given in F1 and F5–F7. Those for second_day, third_day and fourth_day are approved only once the required changes are made. All 31 anim_zemirot stanza URNs are approved.
